brief: Check CreateIssue and its API route in this Gitea revision against the independently supplied current policy. Compare authenticated repository readers and principals with issue write permission. Trace route-level controls, repository or issue-unit checks and the issue creation effect; identify any relevant exceptions instead of assuming endpoint-local checks are the whole path. Explain policy compliance and precise source or deployment limits.

policy.text: Creating an issue requires write permission to the repository's issues unit. Read permission to the repository alone does not authorize this write.

behavior.explanation: For the reviewed API path, an authenticated principal with read permission to the target repository's issues unit can reach issue creation even without issues-unit write permission. The route requires a token, a non-archived repository, valid request binding, and reqRepoReader(unit.TypeIssues), but not a writer guard. reqRepoReader accepts issues-unit read permission and also explicitly accepts repository administrators and site administrators. In CreateIssue, CanWrite(unit.TypeIssues) only controls deadline, milestone, assignees, and labels; the non-writer branch merely clears labels and then still calls issue_service.NewIssue. The issue is bound to ctx.Repo.Repository and its poster to ctx.Doer, and NewIssue delegates creation to issues_model.NewIssue inside a transaction. Thus repository read alone authorizes the core write on this path, contrary to the supplied policy.

branches.condition: Authenticated principal; target repository is accepted by mustNotBeArchived; request binding succeeds; ctx.Repo.Permission.CanRead(unit.TypeIssues) is true; ctx.Repo.Permission.CanWrite(unit.TypeIssues) is false; no later service exception occurs.
branches.explanation: The POST route uses reqToken and reqRepoReader(unit.TypeIssues), not a writer requirement. The handler omits the deadline, milestone, and assignee processing available to writers and clears requested labels, but it still calls issue_service.NewIssue for ctx.Repo.Repository with ctx.Doer as poster. This is the policy-violating decisive branch.

branches.condition: Authenticated principal has issues-unit write permission and satisfies the other route and service conditions.
branches.explanation: Creation proceeds, and the handler additionally accepts the deadline and processes milestone, assignees, and labels, subject to assignee validation and service errors. This branch is allowed by the supplied policy, but it does not cure the reader-only branch.

branches.condition: Principal lacks issues-unit read permission and is neither a repository administrator nor a site administrator.
branches.explanation: reqRepoReader returns HTTP 403 before the handler. This is a read-level denial, not enforcement of the policy's required write threshold.

branches.condition: Principal lacks the specific CanRead(unit.TypeIssues) result but IsUserRepoAdmin() or IsUserSiteAdmin() is true, and all other route/service conditions pass.
branches.explanation: reqRepoReader expressly exempts repository and site administrators from its specific-read test. No separate write check gates core creation in CreateIssue. Whether those administrator predicates always imply normative issues-unit write authority is not established by the reviewed bodies, so this is a relevant explicit route exception rather than assumed equivalence.

branches.condition: The issue poster is blocked by the repository owner or by a requested assignee.
branches.explanation: issue_service.NewIssue checks blocking before entering the creation transaction and returns ErrBlockedUser; the API handler maps that error to HTTP 403. This service-level exception applies beyond the endpoint-local reader check.

branches.condition: A writer supplies a nonexistent or non-assignable assignee, or an assignee lookup/access check fails.
branches.explanation: The handler returns before NewIssue when assignee resolution or assignability validation fails. Reader-only principals do not enter this assignee-processing branch because assignee IDs remain empty.

branches.condition: reqToken rejects the request, or mustNotBeArchived rejects the target repository.
branches.explanation: Both controls are attached to this POST before CreateIssue. Their implementations were not read here, so this branch records the route-visible short-circuit without claiming unreviewed detailed semantics.

missing.detail: The implementations of reqToken, mustNotBeArchived, route execution/short-circuit ordering, and the complete enclosing issue-scope/repository-assignment middleware chain were not read. The route visibly names reqToken and mustNotBeArchived, but detailed authentication, archive, token-scope, and upstream repository-loading behavior is therefore not fully established. This does not remove the decisive reader-only path shown by the route and handler once those prerequisites pass.
missing.nextRead: Read the definitions of reqToken and mustNotBeArchived in routers/api/v1/api.go, plus the remainder of the enclosing /repos issue group and its repoAssignment/checkTokenPublicOnly/tokenRequiresScopes middleware registration.

missing.detail: services/issue.NewIssue calls issues_model.NewIssue inside a transaction, but the body of models/issues.NewIssue was not read. The source establishes the intended creation effect and transactional delegation, but not every database mutation or model-level validation.
missing.nextRead: Read the NewIssue implementation in models/issues/issue.go and directly called issue-creation helpers.

missing.detail: The derivation of ctx.Repo.Permission, ctx.Repo.Repository, ctx.Doer, IsUserRepoAdmin, and IsUserSiteAdmin was not traced. Therefore the exact permission aggregation rules and whether administrator status necessarily implies issues-unit write permission remain unverified.
missing.nextRead: Read repository assignment and API context construction in services/context/repo.go and services/context/api.go, and permission/admin predicate implementations in models/perm/access and services/context.

missing.detail: No evidence establishes that a running Gitea deployment uses exactly revision fc28937a8d772fe9e4025c9b5f24d5db4d86610b, has no downstream patches, or has equivalent routing/configuration. The conformance finding is source-visible for this revision only.

policyAssessment.explanation: The independent policy requires issues-unit write permission and says repository read alone is insufficient. This revision's reviewed create-issue API route admits authenticated issues-unit readers, and its handler still performs the creation call when CanWrite(unit.TypeIssues) is false. Write permission expands which metadata can be supplied; it is not a prerequisite for creating the issue itself.

candidate.scope: Source-visible conformance review of POST /repos/{username}/{reponame}/issues and routers/api/v1/repo.CreateIssue in go-gitea/gitea@fc28937a8d772fe9e4025c9b5f24d5db4d86610b only; no claim of all-repository or deployed-instance coverage.
